subject: MAP: Cost validation & eval timeline — tokens/$, caching & batching assumptions
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Cost validation & eval timeline — tokens/$, caching & batching assumptions

Alex — thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our MAP kickoff, attaching the working cost assumptions and the evaluation timeline we discussed. High-level notes below so we have a single source of truth for procurement and engineering to validate: 

1) Tokens per call assumptions
   - Average prompt length (user input + system instructions): 300 tokens
   - Average generated length: 220 tokens
   - Baseline tokens/interaction: 520 tokens

2) Pricing assumptions (tokens/$) — these are conservative for procurement
   - Hosted SKU: 50,000 tokens / $1 (approx $0.00002/token)
   - Dedicated estimate (after reserved discount): 200M tokens / $1,000 monthly commit

3) Caching & batching levers to hit target unit cost
   - Prefix (system + prompt) caching expected to save ~18% on typical 1:1 flows
   - KV cache re-use for multi-turn dialogs -> reduces generation tokens by up to 30% in prototypes
   - Intelligent batching (10–30ms queuing window) for low-latency bursts estimated to reduce per-token GPU costs by ~12% at 50 RPS

4) Eval plan & gates
   - Week 1: smoke tests (latency/throughput) with 1k sessions/day
   - Week 2: MAP-run – functional accuracy on 200 prompts + cost validation at production QPS
   - Acceptance gate: average tokens/$ within 15% of projection and zero P0 quality regressions

Next steps: Ben to confirm commercial framing for the reserved commit, Karthik to validate batching/caching feasibility with infra, and Alex to confirm procurement timeline. I've attached the spreadsheet with per-flow breakdowns.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0191

Attachments: helixmed_map_cost_assumptions_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval-plan-schedule.pdf (pdf)

Vanessa — appreciate this. A few clarifying questions from engineering/procurement after reviewing the sheet:

- Can you call out which of the caching numbers are validated on Redwood Dedicated vs hosted? Our security team prefers Dedicated for PHI flows.
- For the batching estimate, how long is the queuing window assumed to be? We want to ensure latency stays <300ms p95.

Procurement is targeting a decision by next Friday (2025-08-29). Can we get a short addendum that lists the assumptions that procurement should include in their SOW/PO?

Date: 2025-08-21T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Cost validation & eval timeline — batching/cache feasibility notes

Ben / Vanessa — quick infra confirmation after poking at the sample trace you shared: 

- Token counting: Redwood billing only counts tokens sent to the LLM runtime (prompt + generated). We can add a note to exclude UI telemetry from billable tokens; that needs to be enforced at the client side or at the proxy.
- Caching: Prefix caching is supported on both Hosted and Dedicated. On Dedicated, we can enable longer TTLs for KV caching and prioritize cache-resident requests on the serving pool (reduces GPU cycles). From our internal sims, enabling prefix+KV for HelixMed's dialog mix reduces billable generation tokens by ~26% (range 18–32 depending on turn length).
- Batching: To maintain <300ms p95, a dynamic batching window of 8–12ms is appropriate for steady traffic; during bursts we fall back to smaller windows. At 50–150 RPS the effective per-token cost drops ~10–15% from batching; at very low QPS (<5 RPS) batching doesn't help.

I'll annotate the attached spreadsheet with the sim numbers. For procurement: recommend including a 90-day trial commit with a measured burn-down clause tied to observed tokens/$ in weeks 2–4 of the eval.

Karthik
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the questions and the tight timeline. Attached is a two-page addendum draft and an annotated cost sheet (helixmed_map_cost_assumptions_v1.xlsx). Highlights: 

- Billing definition: "Billable tokens" = prompt tokens + model-generated tokens. UI metadata (timestamps, client-side logs) are excluded and should be stripped by the HelixMed proxy before calls.
- Dedicated vs Hosted notes: numbers in the sheet show conservative hosted economics; Dedicated commit pricing line items are highlighted in yellow and include the recommended 30% burst buffer.
- Evaluation acceptance: we propose the MAP gate at the end of Week 2 where HelixMed and Redwood sign off on observed tokens/$ and p95 latency <= 300ms for core flows. If cost deviates >20% from projection, we will run a joint triage and adjust caching/batching/prompt engineering before procurement sign-off.

Action items (next 48h):
- Alex: confirm procurement will accept the addendum language for the SOW/PO (I can run redlines with legal if needed).
- Ben: finalize the committed pricing table and deliver a PO-ready quote.
- Karthik: include the annotated sim tabs and a short note on the operational steps to enable Dedicated cache prioritization.

If everyone is aligned, we lock the MAP timeline (Week 1 smoke + Week 2 MAP-run) and procurement targets next Friday (08/29).

Best,
Vanessa
